task: open-tennis-robots (flagship row 5): an ESC with its own speed loop

errors.what: first cut of the speed-loop drop fit returned None on every wheel with a constant setpoint (an all-zero W column made the normal equations singular)
errors.fix: drop the column when the setpoint never moves

errors.what: the simulator's 1 ms step advanced revolutions at the end-of-step speed, which read 1.5-3.5% low on a fit exact on its own model
errors.fix: speed-loop plants advance at the step's mean speed; other plants keep the old rule so their recorded sweeps stand (rechecked: unchanged)

doc_friction.issue: the row's buildable list is a run-on of tiny sim refinements; 'an ESC with its own speed loop' was the one item that a builder would hit in practice and it sat last

writeups: ventures/open-tennis-robots/firmware/esp32/README.md (An ESC with its own speed loop)
notes: Simulator: a speed-mode (PI) ESC under the board's WheelLoop rang on 48 of 144 wheels (worst 148% swing, no ball); config.ESC_SPEED_LOOP drops P and keeps 0.5 of I: 0 of 144, worst error 0.05% (tests/speed_esc_sweep.py, eval/speed-esc-sweep-2026-11-18.txt). The existing loop-command drop fit marks every >2% bad speed-mode drop unsure (75 of 75). A closed-form PI-recovery drop fit (tests/speed_loop_fit.py) is exact on its model and within 0.3% unsaturated, but fails once a ball drives the ESC into its current limit, even with the loop surveyed across a drill (eval/speed-loop-survey-2026-11-18.txt); kept off the board. Tests: venture suite via platform/ci/run_venture_tests.py open-tennis-robots (see PR).
